nexus.name: NEXUS
completed: Established specialist-core routing architecture for AI-assisted development.
Created persistent Nexus chat tables with per-user RLS in Supabase.
Created a global in-product Nexus chat with Gamer and admin-only Development modes.
Implemented official multi-provider inference routing with OpenAI, Gemini and Anthropic failover.
Separated inference providers from GitHub, Supabase and Lovable administrative tool bridges.
Configured GPT-5.6 Sol as the default OpenAI model while keeping provider/model selection environment-driven.
Persisted provider/model and relevant specialist cores with assistant messages.
Opened global Gamer chat to anonymous visitors with a ten-successful-response trial and login wall after quota exhaustion.
Added a first-message NEXUS greeting, gamer-native public persona and the original angular N/Z interface mark.
Grounded MGP content recommendations in the live active-games table plus the published content catalog so paused games are not advertised.
Aligned browser and provider timeout budgets so server-side failover can finish before the client abandons a reply.
inProgress: Connect scoped GitHub, Supabase Management API and Lovable MCP credentials to executable Nexus tools.
next: Configure at least one official inference API credential in deployment secrets and test live model replies end to end.
Add the GitHub App bridge as the first write-capable Nexus development tool using branch/review/merge by default.
Add explicit human-approval gates before destructive or production-impacting tool actions.
Consider an opt-in multi-model council mode only for difficult admin tasks after normal failover is stable.

aegis.name: AEGIS
completed: Restricted Nexus Development mode to MGP administrators.
Kept model-provider credentials server-side and documented that consumer sessions must not be used as hidden API credentials.
Applied per-user RLS to Nexus conversations and optimized Nexus auth.uid() RLS evaluation.
Protected anonymous Nexus storage from direct browser access with deny RLS policies and revoked anon/authenticated grants.
Added server-side guest quota enforcement, atomic assistant-response counting and a short-window per-session rate limit.
next: Review GitHub App, Supabase Management API and Lovable MCP scopes before enabling Nexus write actions.
Add approval and audit records for privileged Nexus tool execution.

veil.name: VEIL
completed: Scoped Nexus authenticated chat history to the user through RLS.
Separated Gamer mode from internal Development context to avoid exposing repository/admin details to normal users.
Implemented anonymous Nexus sessions with an opaque HTTP-only cookie rather than email or device fingerprinting.
Set anonymous trial records to expire after 30 days and added automated daily deletion of expired guest sessions/messages.
Added UI disclosure that guest messages may be processed by MGP's configured official AI providers.
next: Define user-facing deletion/export controls for authenticated Nexus conversation history.
Keep provider-data disclosure updated if optional multi-provider council features are introduced.

atlas.name: ATLAS
completed: Added explicit source attribution metadata to Dark Souls and Dark Souls III boss artwork mappings.
Preferred identifiable concept/reference artwork over ambiguous screenshots where practical.
Preserved source-page links for externally sourced boss artwork.
Recorded NEXUS brand provenance and kept personal legal identifiers out of source control.
Stored the first NEXUS N/Z mark as original editable vector geometry in the project.
Defined the AVAPGV licensing-report rule that public accessibility is not treated as permission to reuse external media.
next: Continue replacing weak fallback artwork when higher-quality, clearly sourced assets are found.
Keep provenance metadata attached to every new external media source.
Keep any formal NEXUS trademark/copyright/business registrations in private legal records rather than the client repository.
blocked: Some bosses still lack a sufficiently reliable boss-specific asset from currently reviewed sources.

pulse.name: PULSE
next: Track model IDs and provider API changes so Nexus defaults do not become stale.
Track game/editorial data that can become stale and define refresh expectations before automating it.

gear.name: GEAR
completed: Registered GitHub, Supabase and Lovable as separate Nexus tool bridges with explicit transports and approval requirements.
Scheduled a daily pg_cron retention job to delete expired anonymous Nexus sessions and cascading message history.
Standardized AVAPGV Watch on a responsive branded MG Profile HTML email contract with plain-text fallback and secret-safe reporting.
next: Implement scoped OAuth/App credential flows for Nexus administrative tools.
Identify repeated manual project workflows that are stable enough to automate.
Coordinate with PULSE when recurring content or data refreshes are introduced.
blocked: No dedicated multi-agent/background-worker runtime exists yet for independent specialist agents.

vector.name: VECTOR
completed: Separated boss-card framing from boss-detail framing so each context can use its own crop and scale.
Added per-boss image position, scale and cover/contain controls for Dark Souls and Dark Souls III.
Reduced poor letterboxing for landscape boss screenshots by allowing targeted crop/zoom.
Changed the games catalog to a denser responsive grid while preserving the homepage carousel.
Made Nexus multi-provider behavior failover-first instead of querying every model for every message, limiting unnecessary latency and cost.
Bound anonymous Nexus replies to shorter message/output limits and a finite ten-response trial to control public inference cost.
Reduced the per-provider timeout and increased the browser inference window so failover has a bounded path without premature client aborts.
next: Review external boss-art delivery for image weight, caching and layout stability after visual approval.
Profile Nexus latency and provider failure rates before adding parallel council inference.
Profile high-cost routes before proposing additional performance work.
